description: XGBoost trained on the exp006 (DTW) feature set. The exp006 LightGBM result was 36.394; running an XGBoost on the same features tests whether tree algorithm choice matters and — more importantly — produces diverse OOF predictions for later stacking. Stacking gains usually come from algorithmic diversity, not feature diversity, when one feature set dominates.
implementation_notes: Use the EXACT same feature matrix as exp006 — load it via the function added to src/features.py.
XGBoost params: device='cuda', tree_method='hist', max_depth=8, eta=0.05, subsample=0.85, colsample_bytree=0.85, min_child_weight=8, n_estimators=4000 with early_stopping_rounds=100.
5-fold GroupKFold by well_id. Save OOF and test predictions matching the row order of train and test CSVs.
Compare to exp006 (LGBM 36.394). Whatever the result, the OOF is needed for stacking — so this experiment is valuable even if RMSE is slightly worse, as long as it's competitive (within ~1 RMSE).
